purpose: Bounded authoring reference for replacing disposable Prototype bindings with owned skill tools. This is not an application template or an additional WebUI schema.

binding_rules.tool_declarations: Expose each callable with @tool in the skill manifest entry module (use a thin decorated wrapper when implementation lives in another module), and list it in exports.tools and tools with its entry and input/output schemas. Reads declare side_effects=none; mutations declare accurate write effects. A tool-backed browser data route declares route=tool, tool, first_paint, recovery, guard_visibility, budget.max_payload_bytes and a causal read_policy OBJECT, not a string. See examples.tool_data_route: mode, triggers, max_request_hz and preserve_last_value are required; targeted_invalidation is a trigger and its invalidation_tags belong INSIDE read_policy. No live polling. In skill.yaml, data_routes[*].tool is the LOCAL declared name, e.g. list_records. In WebUI, dataSource.name and callSkill.target are QUALIFIED, e.g. sample_skill.list_records. Do not interchange these namespaces.
binding_rules.package_tests: Skill tests run in the isolated package; sibling scenarios/projects are absent. Cross-component UI/manifest checks belong in scenario tests in the admitted application closure. ADAOS_REPO_ROOT is an authoring aid, not an installed-skill contract; tests cannot require a repository checkout. Subprocesses use sys.executable and inherited SDK PYTHONPATH; never rebuild it. Move checks to their owner, not skips. Use temporary owned data; close SQLite connections because its context manager does not. Scenario tests assert owned semantics, not absence of checkpoint/materializer fields. scenario.json may embed ui.application/version; verify equivalence with webui.json, not an exact minimal ui mapping.
binding_rules.source_edits: Use Unicode-safe file edits. On Windows PowerShell, piping source code through the default external-command encoding can replace non-ASCII literals with question marks even when the output file is UTF-8. Prefer apply_patch for edits and UTF-8 script files for structured rewrites; do not pipe localized source literals through a default-encoded shell. Preserve existing localization and current user language.
binding_rules.related_choices: A form choice field may declare optionsDataSource with kind=skill, name=<owned_skill>.<read_tool>, params and invalidationTags, or kind=mcp with an admitted public Root MCP toolId, arguments, dryRun=true and resultPath. Add optionValuePath=id and optionLabelPaths=[name]. Return an array or {items:[...]}. The loader shares the normal causal read/cache/retry path; it never submits writes. Unavailable or malformed choices block writable submission without clearing the draft. Do not copy authoritative installation, identity, role, or permission records into static options.
binding_rules.dynamic_editor: A trusted dataSource may project typed form fields inside selected records. Declare inputs.recordsPath, fieldsPath and valuesPath plus selectedStateKey. Only inert field declarations and values come from data; actions remain package-owned, and provider-supplied option sources or upload/read targets are stripped. Preserve the complete selected record as $event.record and take identity, release digest, component and expected revision from it. A missing/malformed fieldsPath blocks submission. See examples.dynamic_record_editor.
binding_rules.read: Use dataSource.kind=skill and name=<owned_skill>.<exported_tool>. params accepts $state references. Return a collection as {items:[...]} and one record directly or as {item:{...}}. ui.form requires records with id and an explicit inputs.selectedStateKey for skill sources. Empty selection is create mode, not the first returned record. A get tool should return an empty item for empty id.
binding_rules.selection: Keep accepted selection/navigation. Set the selected id before opening the editor; use it in inputs.selectedStateKey and dataSource.params.id. item.details actions sharing a named on=click:<command> run in order, stopping on false/throw. Label one step for one button. Generic on=click buttons stay independent.
binding_rules.board_move: collection.board on=move spreads displayed item fields at event top level. Include revision in reads and bind $event.revision, not $event.record.revision. See examples.board_move. Added fields: fromLaneId, toLaneId, previousIndex, currentIndex, interaction, laneKey, patch. Lane is already optimistic; fromLaneId is its prior value. Revision is unchanged. Awaited callSkill false/denied result or throw rolls back the move. The lane selector uses the same event. Never fetch a fresh revision during a move to bypass stale-view conflict detection.
binding_rules.creation: For state-initialized creation, use a separate ui.form without dataSource. Before openModal, updateState with draft-specific field keys, clearing old draft values and setting the chosen parent. Fields bind via stateKey (alias state_key); without it the key is form.<widget.id>.<field.id>, not field.id. defaultValue/default/value are literal values, not $state expressions. A dataSource form does not hydrate fields from page state; an empty selected id ignores its returned record. Do not use a get tool's empty-id response to initialize a child. Use a dropdown with related_choices for a visible parent caption, or explicitly bind a known read-only caption alongside the parent id. No selection must offer a parent choice or disable creation, not show an unexplained empty read-only field.
binding_rules.mutation: callSkill.target=<owned_skill>.<exported_tool>. $event.values=draft; $event.record=loaded id/revision. Never bind revision to editable fields or invent caller identity. inputs.buttons[*].id runs actions with the SAME id in order; on=submit alone does not bind steps. Post-success updateState shares that id. False/throw/cancel stops later steps. interaction.submit.defaultAction selects Enter's button. Keep unrelated mutations on distinct buttons.
binding_rules.result: Client unwraps the HTTP tool envelope to the handler result. Action resultStateKey writes this result into page state; action resultPath optionally projects within it, e.g. item, not result.item. This projection does not apply to a skill dataSource: return the shape the widget consumes. Declare invalidates on mutations matching dataSource.invalidationTags to refresh affected reads only. Prefer entity/projection tags over one app-wide tag; include relationship dependencies when derived captions, choices or locks change. Test that every changed consumer is refreshed, not a prescribed tag spelling. A callSkill action used for reading or issuing an editor token must declare invalidates:[]: omission uses the legacy GLOBAL refresh default, even for a tool with side_effects=none. Avoid this read-triggered fanout; never suppress invalidation of an actual write.
binding_rules.failure: A thrown handler error, failed transport, or returned {ok:false,error:<code>,message:<human reason>} rejects the command. Form commands await completion even if background=true. A denied/skipped command or pending approval is not form success. inputs.closeOnSuccess with explicit buttons closes only after success; leave resetOnSuccess false to retain a failed draft. Server enforces rights, invariants and revision conflicts independently of UI enabledIf/readOnlyIf. Do not return ok:true for an unsuccessful mutation.
binding_rules.authorization: Call adaos.sdk.access.require('workspace.read') or require('workspace.write') inside each tool BEFORE touching data. Use adaos.sdk.access.caller() only for verified caller attribution. An absent caller is not owner. Personal DEV preview uses the same /api/tools/call ingress: the Client supplies its existing node-owner credential, Core verifies it and propagates the owner identity into the selected DEV skill handler. The app does not configure this transport, create grants, inject identity or require installation to use this owner path. Owner-issued scoped session credentials admit only their named installed skill; they are deliberately rejected in personal DEV. DEV-owner acceptance therefore cannot prove delegated reader/writer access. Application unit tests may isolate the SDK access boundary and assert denials; independent Core/HTTP tests qualify real ingress. No custom authentication or role registry belongs in the app.
binding_rules.persistence: Use adaos.sdk.data.skill_env.skill_data_root() for owned durable data, outside source/package files. Standard-library sqlite3 is allowed for atomic relationships, optimistic revisions and app-owned business rules. New installation starts empty; keep representative Prototype records only in tests. Add versioned compatible schema initialization/migration and persistence tests. The SDK resources facade does not register arbitrary transaction handlers.
binding_rules.google_gmail: For Google Gmail use only adaos.sdk.providers.gmail. The Core adapter owns OAuth state, PKCE, access/refresh tokens, refresh and the fixed gmail.googleapis.com destination. Skills must not use requests/httpx, adaos.sdk.net.external_api, secrets slots or arbitrary URLs for Gmail. The accepted Prototype already owns and registers its package-neutral semantic intent; preserve pageSchema.meta.builder.cbs_intent and do not invent another intent-registration path. If a compatible installed contract is supplied in portable_contract_reuse, preserve its exact semantic identity and schemas. For a second consumer, expose reusable_connections and attach_reusable_connection as explicit setup tools before offering a fresh OAuth flow; discovery must not attach an account, and neither operation returns or copies credentials. Author contracts/provider.cbs.yaml only when the candidate owns a new physical provider implementation. The trusted package compiler emits canonical contracts and the trusted Builder worker owns PackageRelease closure, production resolution and admission after candidate validation. Candidate source must not call runtime-backed developer validation, publication, compilation or admission APIs.
binding_rules.attachments: Prototype and production attachment storage are different contracts. fileStorage=prototype uploads only to disposable Preview resource storage. For durable app-owned bytes, declare storage.blob in the skill and Project permission profile, use fileStorage=skill, and set qualified uploadTarget and readTarget from the same owned skill. The upload tool is a mutating tool with narrow permissions [storage.blob, workspace.write], application_access permission workspace.write, and it calls adaos.sdk.data.blob.put_upload(<logical-store>) exactly once; bytes never appear in arguments. It returns that blob receipt directly or under blob. The read tool is read-only with narrow permissions [storage.blob, workspace.read], application_access permission workspace.read, accepts ref plus optional field_id/webspace_id, and returns {ok:true,ref:<the exact requested sha256 ref>} after applying app rules; Core then serves the verified content-addressed object. Form fields should set maxBytes <= 10485760 and an image accept filter when appropriate. Persist the returned /api/tools/... attachment reference in owned relational data and render it through normal media/attachment fields. Without fileStorage, forms collect metadata only. Missing upload/read tools, storage.blob, exact permission declarations, byte persistence tests, denied-writer tests, or authenticated read evidence is a blocking capability gap; never present metadata as an uploaded file or weaken the accepted requirement silently.
binding_rules.discovery: The supplied owned skill manifest and handlers define the local tool declaration pattern. Add tools to its exports and declarations with accurate read/write side effects; never infer caller rights from those effects. Consult targeted public SDK descriptors only for contracts still missing after this capsule. Preserve the accepted workflows, not Prototype storage or sample records. Larger new UX choices need review, not extra speculative hard acceptance requirements.

external_provider.title: Gmail account
external_provider.purpose: Read, organize, trash and send mail requested by the user.

native_cbs.operation_mapping: Map every accepted semantic mail operation exactly once to an existing tools[].name. Do not copy input_schema or output_schema into the descriptor; the compiler takes them from skill.yaml. Declare bounded errors for every operation.

semantic_intent.candidate_action: preserve exactly; do not register, copy into the provider descriptor, or select a package in the semantic Application

lifecycle.validation: Run focused package tests only. Do not call adaos.sdk.developer.validation from the isolated model process because it has no AgentContext. Returning the bounded source is sufficient; the trusted worker compiles, validates and admits it.

capability.title: Manage mail messages
invariants: credentials and OAuth tokens never cross the Core provider boundary
one application command id causes at most one provider send call
mail content remains transient and is not persisted by the binding
effects: read and organize mail through the explicitly connected account
send mail only after an explicit user command

skill_manifest.tool_rules: Each public tool declares narrow permissions, accurate side_effects and application_access.permission=providers.google.gmail. Read tools use read_only/none; label, archive, trash and send tools use external_write. Require workspace.read/write first when the tool also reads or mutates app-owned state.

sdk.send_semantics: Create an RFC 2822 message and URL-safe base64 encode it without persisting body text. Deduplicate the user command in app-owned storage before the single SDK call. Core never automatically retries a send.
sdk.error: Catch gmail.GmailProviderError. Its public fields are code:str, status_code:int|null and retryable:bool; to_dict() returns {ok:false,error:<code>,status_code,retryable}. Do not expose exception causes or remote response bodies.

begin_connection.persistence: authorization_url and OAuth state are ephemeral; do not persist or log them

connection_status.missing: A missing connection raises GmailProviderError(code='gmail_account_not_connected'); map it to the accepted disconnected/setup-required UI state.

operation.rule: The owned skill validates and projects result into its own bounded output schema. It never returns or persists a raw provider object that is not required by the accepted UI.

success_envelopes.list_message_summaries_result: {messages:[Gmail metadata message],nextPageToken?:string,fetch_strategy:'gmail_http_batch',network_round_trips:1|2,omitted_message_ids?:[string]}; use this bounded progressive operation for first-paint lists instead of list_messages followed by N get_message calls
success_envelopes.get_message_result: The Gmail users.messages.get object. Project only id, threadId, labelIds, snippet and decoded headers/body fields required for the selected transient reader; never log or persist payload body data.
success_envelopes.modify_or_trash_result: The resulting Gmail message object; project only confirmation identity and current labels.
success_envelopes.send_message_result: {id:string,threadId:string,labelIds?:[string]}; treat success only after this envelope is returned. A transport failure is not a confirmed send.

data.description: URL-safe base64 MIME body bytes; transiently decode in the owning skill and never log or persist the value.

send_uncertain.rule: Keep the app-owned idempotency record pending/unknown and require explicit reconciliation; do not automatically call send_message again.

steps: when disconnected, call an owned reusable_connections projection and offer each redacted account as an explicit Attach existing account action
the attach action calls an owned attach_reusable_connection mutation; never attach during first paint or account discovery
if no reusable account is available, offer a fresh OAuth connection
call the owned begin_connection tool with resultStateKey=gmailConnection and invalidates:[]
on the same button command, openUrl with url=$state.gmailConnection.authorization_url, target=_blank and withAuth=false
refresh connection_status after the user returns; expose disconnected, connected, denied, expired and provider-unavailable states

failure_contract.read_projection_rule: A tool used as a browser dataSource must convert expected provider lifecycle errors into a successful bounded projection: connection_status returns {ok:true,items:[{id:'google.gmail',status:'disconnected|auth_required|permission_denied|offline|provider_error',least_privilege_note:string}]}; list_labels, list_messages, list_message_summaries and get_message return {ok:true,items:[],status:<the same lifecycle state>,notice:string}. Do not retain ok:false when adding items. This lets the accepted setup/authorization/offline UI settle without treating an expected state as a transport failure.
failure_contract.rule: Mutations, invalid input and unexpected provider failures return {ok:false,error,message} or raise a bounded error. Never return a successful mutation after provider failure and never include response bodies, tokens or OAuth codes in logs/errors.

tests: mock the typed SDK facade; package tests perform no external network calls
prove missing Application context and missing/denied provider capability fail closed
prove search/list/list_message_summaries/get/labels and every accepted mutation map to the exact SDK method
prove send idempotency suppresses a duplicate before a second SDK call
prove tokens, OAuth codes and message bodies are absent from logs, persisted UI state and fixtures

production_attachment.purpose: Persist app-owned immutable bytes behind normal Application authorization without placing bytes or base64 in JSON tool calls.

limits.filename: 1..200 safe characters with no slash, backslash, colon or control character
limits.mime_policy: The browser accept filter is UX only. The upload tool must reject MIME types outside the application's allowlist before put_upload().

webui_field.target_rules: Both targets are qualified <skill>.<tool> names, belong to the same owned skill and are distinct tools. maxBytes is positive and no greater than core_max_bytes.

upload_tool.invocation: Core invokes this declared tool only through PUT /api/tools/{skill}/{upload_tool}/attachments after caller authentication and binary admission.
handler_order: validate field_id, media_type and the application's narrower size policy from admitted metadata
return the receipt directly or as {blob:<receipt>}

ref.description: Internal adaos-blob identity; do not persist this as the UI field value.

digest.description: Must equal the admitted input digest.

size_bytes.description: Must equal the admitted body length.

upload_tool.one_use: A second put_upload() in the same invocation raises and must not be retried inside the tool.

browser_receipt.persistence: The Client places ref, not blob_ref, into the file field before the form save action. Persist that string in owned relational data. A single-valued field is a string; multiple=true produces an array of strings.
browser_receipt.failure: A failed upload leaves the previous field value and editor open. A failed record save must also preserve the previous persisted photo reference.

read_tool.invocation: Core invokes this declared tool before GET serves the content-addressed object.
handler_order: require workspace.read before any storage lookup
apply app-owned visibility rules without trusting caller fields in arguments
return {ok:true,ref:<the exact requested sha256 ref>} when authorized

permission_matrix.read: allow when the record is visible

production_attachment.lifecycle: Blob objects and relational references are both skill-owned runtime data. Stable-to-Beta forward migration copies/adopts them as one governed dataset; source/package files never contain uploaded bytes.

tool_data_route.first_paint: empty until the authorized read completes
tool_data_route.recovery: explicit retry; preserve the last successful value
tool_data_route.guard_visibility: show the read error without reporting success

rejected_write.message: The record changed. Reopen it before saving.
